Subject: Post-demo: capacity hypothesis, benchmark schedule, and acceptance criteria

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + proposal so we have a single mutual-action plan to move the pilot forward. Key points we agreed on in the demo:

- Target production SLOs: p95 end-to-end response latency below ~300ms for short interactive calls; streaming sessions for long completions should remain responsive (see below).
- Expected steady-state concurrency: ~40–60 concurrent active users during business hours, with short bursts up to ~300 RPS at peak.
- Typical request: ~400–800 tokens (most ~600 tokens) with streaming enabled for multi-chunk outputs.

Proposed next steps (hypothesis-driven):
1) We run a 2-week pilot to validate SLOs under representative traffic.
2) Redwood will provision a reserved pool mapped to two candidate GPU configurations (H100 and A100) for side-by-side benchmarking.
3) We'll run an agreed benchmark harness (streaming-capable load generator + prefix caching on realistic prompts).
4) Acceptance criteria: sustained 95th percentile latency <= 300ms for interactive flows, p95 streaming chunk latency <= 220ms, and sustained token throughput to meet your estimated monthly ceiling.

Can you confirm the rough monthly token budget and whether the 300 RPS burst is a hard requirement or a 5–10 minute rarity? Also attaching a draft benchmark schedule and the capacity hypothesis table we plan to use.

I'll loop in Karthik and Ben on the technical plan; they will propose the exact GPU mapping and runbook.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Post-demo: capacity hypothesis, benchmark schedule, and acceptance criteria

Thanks Markus —

Appreciate the write-up, that aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from the product side:

- Monthly token budget: roughly 1.6B tokens (Q4 planning).
- Peak bursts: 300 RPS is our design ceiling for marketing-driven spikes; these could last ~10 minutes and aren't continuous. We care most about steady-state responsiveness during business hours (40–60 concurrent).
- Streaming requirements: p95 chunk-to-chunk latency needs to be low because our UX stitches partial answers live. Target p95 chunk latency <= 250ms for ~512-token chunks; end-to-end p95 for short requests should be under 350ms.

Questions for your team:
1) Can you map the pilot to specific GPU SKUs (H100 / A100 / L4) and expected sustained RPS for a 600-token average with streaming?
2) What does Redwood recommend for reserved throughput headroom vs expected steady-state? (i.e., 1.5x to 2x safety factor?)
3) We'll need SOC2 audit artifacts and network ACL list before we start workload testing — can you share the doc bundle?

If you can provide the GPU mapping and a proposed pilot start date next week, we can book the windows.

Best,
Samantha Lopez
Head of Product, Finlytics
samantha@finlytics.com

Hi Samantha — looping in the technical details and a concrete hypothesis so we can lock the pilot scope.

Summary (short): based on your average request size ~600 tokens with streaming, and the latency targets you provided, our bench estimates map to the following ballpark sustained requests-per-second per GPU (streaming-enabled):

- NVIDIA H100 (80GB): ~120–150 RPS sustained (per-GPU) for 600-token streaming flows with prefix caching and optimized kernels. p95 chunk latency estimate: ~180–240ms depending on chunk size and network egress.
- NVIDIA A100 (80GB): ~70–100 RPS sustained. p95 chunk latency estimate: ~240–320ms.
- L4-class (small inference GPU): ~25–40 RPS sustained; better cost but higher latency variance.

Pilot recommendation:
- Reserve a 2-GPU pool and run comparative benchmarks: 2x H100 vs 2x A100 (we can also add an L4 experiment if you want cost data).
- Target configuration for your acceptance criteria: 2x H100 reserved with autoscale cushion for short bursts (target sustained 140 RPS, burst to 300 RPS with short-term buffer across the pool).
- Safety factor: we suggest 1.6x reserved headroom above expected steady-state to account for request-size variance and concurrent users.

Acceptance test plan (we attach a short bench harness spec):
- Test harness: custom streaming client that simulates real client-side chunking + KV cache warm-up. We'll run ramp windows: 5m warmup, 20m steady at target load, 10m spike to burst.
- Metrics: p95 end-to-end, p95 per-chunk latency, sustained token/s throughput, GPU utilization, and token cost.
- Gate: If p95 end-to-end > 350ms or p95 chunk > 300ms on candidate config, we fail and iterate (either add capacity or change GPU type/quantization).

Attachments included: finlytics_benchmark_plan_v1.xlsx (detailed schedule) and capacity_hypothesis_table.csv (per-GPU throughput numbers).

Proposed pilot kickoff: Wednesday 26 Aug 2026 — Redwood will provision the pools in the morning and run the first comparative run that afternoon. Please let us know if that works for you and provide the list of CIDR blocks for test traffic so we can open ACLs.

Thanks,
